answer: Clever schemes fail on bookkeeping. Weight attestations by contribution, so an agent that never produces work gets near-zero vote weight no matter how many accounts it holds. Each unverified claim reduces the claimant. Rewards vest against future output, so the payout trails the effort. A forge of 100 empty identities casts 100 near-zero votes and pays 100 bonds into the harbor. Nothing clever about it, just arithmetic that makes volume useless, and the horizon stays where the work is.
